c.tagline: A fairy-tale city of spires and bridges.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town, Charles Bridge and tram 22; taxi, currency-exchange and strip-club scams in the centre

hood_desc: The medieval core around the Astronomical Clock and the Old Town Square, all cobbled lanes, Gothic spires and crowds. Ideal for first-timers who want to be steps from the city's iconic sights, though it is busy and touristy.
The picturesque Lesser Town below Prague Castle, full of baroque palaces, gardens, winding streets and the Charles Bridge approach. Perfect for romantics who want fairytale charm and postcard views.
A grander, more open district built around Wenceslas Square, mixing shopping, hotels, theaters and nightlife. Suits visitors wanting a central, bustling base with commerce and easy transport.
A leafy, upscale residential neighborhood of handsome apartment buildings, parks, wine bars and stylish cafes. Great for those seeking a local, relaxed feel and a strong food and drink scene.

A gritty, bohemian district famous for having the most pubs per capita, plus the towering TV Tower and a lively, alternative nightlife. Best for budget travelers and night owls chasing an authentic, unpolished vibe.
lodging: Hotel U Prince Prague by Bhg

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy tickets via the PID Litacka app, station machines, or a rechargeable Litacka card from DPP info centers; contactless bank-card tap-in is also accepted network-wide. A 30-minute ticket costs 36-39 CZK (~$1.60) and a 24-hour pass 140-150 CZK (~$6.20).
transit.hours: Metro runs about 5am-midnight; night trams and buses run all night at reduced frequency.

landmarks: Charles Bridge
A medieval stone bridge over the Vltava lined with baroque statues, offering the classic postcard view of Prague Castle at sunrise or dusk.
Prague Castle
The largest ancient castle complex in the world, dominating the skyline and seat of Czech rulers for over a thousand years.
Prague Astronomical Clock
A medieval astronomical clock on the Old Town Hall that draws crowds hourly for its Walk of the Apostles show, one of the oldest working clocks of its kind.
Old Town Square
The historic heart of Prague, ringed by colorful baroque buildings, Gothic Tyn Church, and the astronomical clock tower.
St. Vitus Cathedral
A soaring Gothic cathedral within Prague Castle, home to the Bohemian crown jewels and stunning stained-glass windows including one by Alphonse Mucha.
Dancing House
A striking deconstructivist office building nicknamed 'Fred and Ginger' for its swirling, dance-like twin-tower form contrasting with the historic skyline.
Petrin Lookout Tower
A steel lattice tower modeled on the Eiffel Tower atop Petrin Hill, rewarding climbers with sweeping views over Prague's rooftops.
Wenceslas Square
A historic boulevard and site of pivotal moments in Czech history, anchored by the National Museum and the equestrian statue of St. Wenceslas.
Old Jewish Cemetery
A hauntingly beautiful centuries-old burial ground in Josefov with thousands of tightly packed, tilting tombstones layered over generations.
Vltava River and Prague Bridges
The river winding through the city beneath its many historic bridges, forming the scenic backbone of Prague's most photographed cityscape.

train.note: International trains leave from Praha hlavní nádraží (main station). Genuine sleepers run nightly to Zurich and to Košice in eastern Slovakia; everything else listed is a day train. Private operators RegioJet and Leo Express also sell their own tickets on the Vienna, Budapest and Košice routes.

intl.to: Berlin, Vienna, Munich & cities across Europe

bus.note: Most international coaches depart from the ÚAN Florenc terminal (metro B/C); some FlixBus services also call at Hlavní nádraží or Na Knížecí.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked, so there are no international ferries. Boats on the Vltava in Prague are local sightseeing cruises only.

half.name: Karlovy Vary

half.name: Bohemian Switzerland

full.name: Český Krumlov
